title: reduce-gpu-memory-arena-tuning-activation-checkpointing-scratch-buffers
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: long-context and multi-stream workloads were hitting GPU memory OOMs and high workspace footprints under bursty continuous-batching. This PR reduces resident and transient GPU memory pressure by combining three orthogonal approaches: 1) configurable per-block activation checkpointing (selective rematerialization) to trade compute for peak activation memory, 2) reuse of scratch buffers across kernel invocations and tighter lifetimes to cut temporary workspace allocations, and 3) tuning the CUDA/cuMEM arena allocator parameters and introducing a fallback packing policy for small KV cache allocations to reduce fragmentation. The goals are to lower OOM frequency on 16GB/24GB GPUs, reduce the required buffer reservation for the serving runtime, and preserve latency SLOs for common request sizes.

ci_checks: perf-smoke: success (no regressions on baseline burst)
review_comments: Ethan Liu: Nice work - can you add a short rationale for the default checkpointing threshold in defaults.yaml? I worry about increasing tail latency for short requests.
Priya Menon (author): Added comment and tuned the default to only checkpoint for >24 layers or >4k sequence lengths; microbenchmarks show <2% median latency impact for our 8k context profiles.
Marisol Ortega: The scratch buffer pool looks good; suggest adding an assertion in debug builds to detect double-free of temporary buffers.
Priya Menon (author): Added debug-only checks and a unit test that simulates interleaved kernel lifetimes.

Dmitri Petrov: Observed a CI perf-smoke failure on first run (OOM on 24GB test VM) - looks like our arena defaults reserved too little for packed KV cache. Priya: I increased the small-pool reservation and added a fallback that spills smallest cache pages to host when under pressure.
Marisol Ortega: Approved after second perf run. Ethan: Approved. Dmitri: Approved.
release_notes: Reduced GPU peak memory by 18-32% depending on model and sequence length through selective activation checkpointing, scratch buffer reuse, and arena allocator tuning. Added config profile defaults for small/large batch serving. Introduced KV cache packing policy to lower fragmentation. No API changes; runtime flags available behind 'gpu_memory_optimizations' feature flag.
perf_summary: Microbenchmarks across 4 models (7B, 13B, 70B quantized, 70B fp16) and typical request distributions show peak GPU memory reductions of 18%-32% with sustained throughput unchanged for large-batch steady-state; median latency increases 0-3% for very long contexts when checkpointing is enabled but 95th percentile latency impact is mitigated by the selective heuristics. Continuous-batching tests show up to 22% lower transient workspace usage during burst periods.
testing: Added unit tests for scratch_pool lifetime and double-free detection, arena allocator profile unit tests, and integration perf microbench that compares baseline vs optimized profiles. Tests run in CI and on a dedicated perf lab (perf-canary) before merge.
rollback_plan: Feature gated behind 'gpu_memory_optimizations' and controlled by runtime config. If regressions observed, flip feature flag to false and rollback can be performed by cherry-picking revert commit (revert of this PR is cherry-pickable). Detailed rollback steps in docs/perf/gpu-memory-optimizations.md.
notes_for_release_engineering: Default profile set to conservative 'balanced' in defaults.yaml. Release engineering: include perf microbench results and tuned defaults in release notes for next platform patch. Recommend canary rollout on Dedicated clusters for 48-72 hours before wide rollout.
